customSections.text:
SOC-8 (2022) — Current Standard:
• Removed mandatory 12-month real-life experience requirement
• Replaced two-letter requirement with individualized assessment
• Affirms informed consent model for many procedures
• Removed minimum age requirements for many procedures (case-by-case)

SOC-7 (Legacy — still used by many payers):
• Required 2 letters from qualified mental health professionals
• Required 12 months of real-life experience in affirmed gender
• Required 12 months of continuous hormone therapy

⚠ Many payers still use SOC-7 criteria. Obtain both SOC-7 and SOC-8 documentation to maximize approval chances.

raw.markdown:
# Gender-Affirming Urologic Procedures — Authorization Guide

CPT Codes · ICD-10 · WPATH SOC-8 · Payer Requirements

(backHref: /gender-affirming-uro)

## CPT Codes

| CPT | Description | Procedure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 57291 | Construction of artificial vagina; without graft | Vaginoplasty |
| 57292 | Construction of artificial vagina; with graft | Vaginoplasty + graft |
| 55175 | Scrotoplasty; simple | Scrotoplasty |
| 55180 | Scrotoplasty; complicated | Complex scrotoplasty |
| 55970 | Intersex surgery; male to female | MTF genital surgery |
| 55980 | Intersex surgery; female to male | FTM genital surgery |
| 54520 | Orchiectomy, simple | Bilateral orchiectomy |
| 58150 | Total abdominal hysterectomy (corpus and cervix), with or without removal of tube(s), with or without removal of ovary(s) | Hysterectomy |
| 58661 | Laparoscopy, surgical; with removal of adnexal structures (partial or total oophorectomy and/or salpingectomy) | Oophorectomy |
| 53410 | Urethroplasty; 1-stage reconstruction of male anterior urethra | Urethroplasty |

## ICD-10 Diagnoses

| ICD-10 | Description |
| --- | --- |
| F64.0 | Transsexualism (gender dysphoria in adults) |
| F64.8 | Other gender identity disorders |
| F64.9 | Gender identity disorder, unspecified |
| Z87.890 | Personal history of sex reassignment |
| Z76.89 | Encounter for other specified circumstances |
| Q56.4 | Indeterminate sex, unspecified |

Note: ICD-11 uses HA60 (Gender incongruence of adolescence or adulthood) — not yet widely adopted in US billing. Use DSM-5 F64.0 for most US payers.

## Coverage Landscape

### Common Denial Reasons
• "Cosmetic procedure" (incorrect per AMA, AUA, WPATH)
• "Experimental" (incorrect — established procedures with long-term outcomes data)
• Blanket plan exclusion for "sex transformation surgery"
• Insufficient documentation of WPATH criteria
• Missing second mental health letter (legacy SOC-7 requirement)

### Strongest Coverage Arguments
• ACA Section 1557 prohibits sex discrimination in health coverage (includes gender identity)
• AMA, AUA, WPATH, Endocrine Society all classify gender-affirming surgery as medically necessary
• WPATH SOC-8 (2022) is the current international standard of care
• Blanket exclusions for "sex transformation" are increasingly found to violate federal non-discrimination law
• Mental health outcomes data: surgery significantly reduces gender dysphoria and improves quality of life

### Federal and State Protections
• ACA Section 1557: prohibits sex discrimination (includes gender identity) in federally funded health programs
• 22+ states have explicit state laws requiring coverage of gender-affirming care
• Medicare: covers gender-affirming surgery when medically necessary (CMS 2014)
• Medicaid: coverage varies by state; many states now cover gender-affirming care

## Prior Authorization Requirements

### Required Documentation (WPATH SOC-8 / Payer Standard)
• DSM-5 diagnosis of gender dysphoria (F64.0) from qualified mental health provider
• Documentation of persistent, well-documented gender dysphoria
• Mental health evaluation and surgical clearance letter(s)
• Documentation of ≥12 months of hormone therapy (for genital surgery)
• Real-life experience documentation (some payers still require)
• Medical clearance from primary care or endocrinologist
• Two letters of support (legacy SOC-7 — still required by many payers)
• Surgeon's letter of medical necessity with WPATH criteria documentation

### WPATH SOC-8 vs SOC-7 Key Changes
**SOC-8 (2022) — Current Standard:**
• Removed mandatory 12-month real-life experience requirement
• Replaced two-letter requirement with individualized assessment
• Affirms informed consent model for many procedures
• Removed minimum age requirements for many procedures (case-by-case)

**SOC-7 (Legacy — still used by many payers):**
• Required 2 letters from qualified mental health professionals
• Required 12 months of real-life experience in affirmed gender
• Required 12 months of continuous hormone therapy

⚠ Many payers still use SOC-7 criteria. Obtain both SOC-7 and SOC-8 documentation to maximize approval chances.
